questions.question_text:
Petrol costs $189$ c/L.
Express this rate in $\$$/L.

options.why: Divided by $10$ instead of the $100$ cents in a dollar.
Divided by $1000$ instead of $100$.
Multiplied by $100$; cents are smaller than dollars, so the number must get smaller.
Divided by $100$ instead of the $1000$ grams in a kilogram.
Divided by $10$ instead of $1000$.
Multiplied the price by $1000$; each gram must cost less than each kilogram, not more.
Multiplied by $60$ only, which converts seconds to minutes rather than to hours.
Multiplied by $360$ instead of the $3600$ seconds in an hour.
Divided by $3600$; an hour is longer than a second, so more metres are covered, not fewer.
Converted the kilometres but divided by $60$ only, giving metres per minute.
Converted the hour to seconds but left the distance in kilometres.
Multiplied by $3600$ and divided by $1000$, reversing both conversions.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{90\text{ km}}{1\text{ h}}$
$=\frac{(90\times1000)\text{ m}}{(1\times3600)\text{ s}}$
$=\frac{90\,000\text{ m}}{3600\text{ s}}$
$=25\text{ m/s}$

questions.question_text:
A crop yield of $5$ t/ha is converted to kg/m$^2$.
What is the converted rate?

options.why: Used $1$ ha $=100$ m$^2$, forgetting that the length factor of $100$ is squared for area.
Converted the tonnes to kilograms but left the hectare unchanged in the denominator.
Divided by $1\,000\,000$, using the cm$^2$ factor instead of the $10\,000$ m$^2$ in a hectare.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{5\text{ t}}{1\text{ ha}}$
$=\frac{(5\times1000)\text{ kg}}{(1\times10\,000)\text{ m}^2}$
$=\frac{5000\text{ kg}}{10\,000\text{ m}^2}$
$=0.5\text{ kg/m}^2$

questions.question_text:
A machine dispenses $6$ kg/day.
Convert this rate to g/min, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Divided by $60$, as if a day had $60$ minutes instead of $1440$.
Divided by the $24$ hours in a day only, so the answer is per hour, not per minute.
Multiplied by $1440$ and divided by $1000$, reversing both conversions.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{6\text{ kg}}{1\text{ day}}$
$=\frac{(6\times1000)\text{ g}}{(1\times1440)\text{ min}}$
$=\frac{6000\text{ g}}{1440\text{ min}}$
$=4.17\text{ g/min}$
